newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Most analysts positive about LG Metals.
newsitem.headline: Most analysts positive about LG Metals.

text.p: South Korea's LG Metals Corp should follow last week's report of positive earnings and profit in the first half with a solid performance through the rest of the year, analysts said on Monday.
However, they expressed some concerns about the impact of the weakening of the Korean won against the dollar and the company's futures trade.
LG Metals, an affiliate of LG Group, said last week its recurring profit had reached 28.5 billion won in the first half, up from a loss of 7.0 billion won a year earlier.
The company also said sales in the first six months of this year had increased 22 percent to 1.006 trillion won from 827.2 billion won a year ago.

Sam Yang, metals analyst for Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, said he had expected the company would post better-than-expected interim results because of rising copper prices and treatment charges & refining charges in its core refining operations.

"Based on the current situation, I have forecast earnings growth will continue in the second half," Yang said. He has forecast a recurring profit of 58.7 billion won for all of 1997 and a pre-tax profit of 45.3 billion won for the year.

Yang said one of his concerns was the won/dollar rate. Yang based his forecast on an end-year rate of 850 won per dollar. The won stood at 892.10 at midday on Monday and it has been weakening against the dollar in recent weeks.
Yang has given LG Metals a buy-overweight recommendation.
Kim Hee-soo, metals industry analyst for Samsung Securities, said he had expected the company's first-half recurring profit would be closer to 25 billion won.
"The results were a surprise to me because they were higher than I had expected," Kim said.
Similar results were expected in the second half with LG Metals' recurring profit for 1997 as a whole likely to hit Samsung's earlier target of 45 billion won, he said.
"I believe the positive environment for business will add profits to the company. I am sticking to my original forecast," Kim said.
Samsung had a "buy" recommendation for LG Metals before and after the company's earnings announcement. However, Kim said he had not considered the company's futures trade in his forecast.
"LG Metals seems to have done some speculative futures trade, as well as hedging. And I am concerned that they may have increased the volume of their speculative futures trade," he said.
Daewoo Securities was also concerned about the company's futures trade, said an analyst who asked not to be identified.
The Daewoo analyst said he has recommended investors take a "conservative approach" towards LG Metals because of questions about the company's futures operation.
"I was surprised at the result of LG Metals' first half since it was much better than my expectation," he said.
"It is hard to understand that they made a large profit from the unpredictable sector of futures trade," he added.
"If they have hedged against their physical trades, how could they make profit (against their futures positions) every consecutive year," he said.
Analysts said the company's recurring profit from futures trade was 25 billion won in the first half.

The Daewoo analyst said LG Metals had reported a profit from its metals futures trade since 1993. He also said he was concerned about the big increase in LG Metals' futures trade account since last year.

LG Metals' futures trade account surged to 120.4 billion won (79.9 billion won profit and 40.5 billion won loss) in 1996 from 21.6 billion won (17.8 billion profit and 3.8 billion loss) in 1995, the Daewoo analyst said.

"We have had some difficulties in analysing LG Metals as its profits and losses from unpredictable sectors such as futures trade have increased significantly when compared to more predictable sectors," he said.

Rumours have swirled for months on the London Metal Exchange (LME) that the company was rolling forward large potential loss-making short futures and options positions. The company has consistently denied the market talk.
Yang of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said he had no worries about the company's futures trade. "The rumours in the market have turned out to be wrong," he said.
